findings.mechanism: 03-timeouts-as-a-first-principle — the DB query has no timeout, so a slow database holds a worker, a DB connection, and memory, potentially saturating the worker pool and the SQLAlchemy/asyncpg connection pool (default size 5) under load.
findings.remediation: Add an explicit timeout to the DB query or configure a statement_timeout on the PostgreSQL side, e.g. `await session.execute(select(1), execution_options={"timeout": 5})` or set `connect_args={"command_timeout": 5}` when creating the async engine.
findings.arithmetic: Workers=4 (Dockerfile uvicorn --workers 4). Default asyncpg/SQLAlchemy pool size per worker=5 (reference 02-connection-pooling-and-pool-exhaustion). Concurrency ceiling = workers × pool_size = 4 × 5 = 20 active DB connections. At request rate 80 rps with DB latency 200 ms, required active connections = rate × latency = 80 × 0.2 s = 16. Worker saturation = 16/20 = 0.8 (80%). Thus under these conditions the service will have ≥80% of its workers blocked by the DB query.
